title: Real Estate Agent on the Go: Why Your Open House Is Losing You Enquiries
excerpt: Open houses lose you calls – an AI receptionist captures every lead, even when you're in the kitchen.
content:
# Real Estate Agent on the Go: Why Your Open House Is Losing You Enquiries

You're doing an open house. Five groups walk through in twenty minutes. You're chatting with the latest couple — they look keen, asking about the kitchen, the backyard — and your phone rings.

You pick it up.

"Hi, I'm calling about the listing on [street name]. What are the rental terms?"

You're standing in someone's kitchen. You can't really talk. You mumble something about texting them back. They hang up. You text them back three hours later. They've already booked an inspection with your competitor.

This happens more than you want to admit.

## The Problem

Real estate is a phone game. Even in 2026, most enquiries still come in as calls. Open-house interest, rental applications, vendor questions, buyer follow-ups. Every single one of them expects someone to answer within the first two rings.

Here's what actually happens:

You're on a showing. Phone goes to voicemail.

You're in a meeting with a client. Goes to voicemail.

You're driving between properties. Goes to voicemail.

It's after 6pm and you've just finished a long day. You didn't even see the missed call notification.

Every time, the caller has two choices: leave a message or call the next agent on the real estate portal. Most people don't leave messages. They call the next agent.

That's not just a missed conversation. That's a missed listing, a missed client, a missed commission.

## What Property Managers Deal With

Property managers have an even worse version of this problem. Tenant emergencies don't care about your schedule. Burst pipes at 7pm. Lockouts at 10pm. "The heating's not working" calls in the middle of winter when you're already handling three other properties.

Your admin can only handle so many calls at once. And outside business hours, there's nobody.

## What We're Building

An AI receptionist that answers every call to your real estate business. Not a voicemail box. An actual conversation.

When a prospective buyer calls about a listing, the AI tells them the key details — price, property type, number of bedrooms, when the next inspection is. If they want to book an inspection, it checks your calendar and books them in. If they're a vendor interested in listing with you, it captures their details and sends you a summary.

For property managers, it triages tenant calls. Urgent emergencies get escalated to you immediately. Routine enquiries — payment questions, maintenance booking, lease details — the AI handles directly.

Your admin still manages the complex conversations. The AI just makes sure no call goes to voicemail.

## Why It Matters for Real Estate

Real estate is competitive enough without losing enquiries because you were busy doing the job. Every unanswered call is someone talking to your competitor instead.

The agents I've spoken to all say the same thing: they didn't realise how many calls they were missing until they actually looked at their phone stats. Some were losing 40-50% of calls during business hours because they were on showings or meetings.

That's not a growth problem. That's a systems problem. And it's one that doesn't require hiring another admin.

## How It Integrates

We're building it to work with the tools you already use. Your CRM, your calendar, your listing management system. The AI doesn't create a new workflow — it fits into what you've already got.

Call comes in. AI answers. Captures details. Books into your calendar. Sends you a notification. You follow up with the lead that's already qualified.

title: How Much Is an Unanswered Call Really Costing Your Business?
excerpt: Every call you miss is money left on the table. Here is how to think about the real cost — and why the fix is cheaper than you think.
content:
# How Much Is an Unanswered Call Really Costing Your Business?

If your business phone rings and nobody picks up, what happens?

Most owners know the answer: the caller leaves voicemail, or worse, hangs up and calls someone else. But very few actually sit down and work out what that is really costing them.

Let me walk through the numbers. Because once you see them, the fix stops feeling like an expense and starts looking like a no-brainer.

## The Simple Math

Take a typical small trade or service business in Melbourne. Say you get 10 phone calls a day. You miss roughly 3 of them — maybe you are on a job, maybe it is after hours, maybe the front desk is busy.

Of those 3 missed calls, let us say 1 in 3 turns into a real job. That is one lost opportunity every single day.

At an average job value of $500, that is $500 a day in unrealised revenue. Over a year, working 250 days, that is $125,000.

That is not a hypothetical. That is what happens when calls go to voicemail and nobody follows up.

## The Hidden Costs

The money is only part of it. Missed calls also mean:

- **Frustrated customers.** Someone rings, gets voicemail, and calls your competitor instead. They are not coming back.
- **Reputation hit.** Google reviews and word of mouth suffer when people feel ignored.
- **Admin time.** Chasing up voicemails, calling people back, trying to work out who was ringing and what they wanted. All of that is time you could spend doing the actual work.

## What a Receptionist Costs

Hiring someone to answer the phone full-time costs at least $60,000 a year in wages, plus super, plus software, plus training. For most small businesses, that is not realistic.

An AI receptionist handles calls 24/7, books appointments, qualifies leads, and sends follow-ups. The cost is a fraction of a full-time salary — and it never takes a sick day.

## The Honest Comparison

I am not going to pretend an AI receptionist replaces a human being. It does not. What it does is catch the calls that would otherwise be lost entirely. It handles the routine stuff — opening hours, bookings, simple questions — so your team can focus on the work that actually needs a human.

Think of it as an extra set of hands that works for free while you sleep.

## The Bottom Line

If you are missing even a handful of calls a week, you are leaving real money on the table. The question is not whether you can afford an AI receptionist. The question is whether you can afford not to have one.

title: What Is an AI Receptionist? A Simple Guide for Busy Small Business Owners
excerpt: If you have heard the term AI receptionist but have no idea what it does — or whether it’s worth it for your business — this guide breaks it down in plain English.
content:
# What Is an AI Receptionist? A Simple Guide for Busy Small Business Owners

You’re on a job. Phone’s buzzing. You either pick up or, more often, miss it.

That missed call is the exact pain point most Australian small‐business owners feel: a call could be a new job, a client question, or a revenue opportunity, and it’s gone.

## What an AI Receptionist Actually Is

An AI receptionist is software that answers your business phone, handles enquiries, books appointments, and sends follow‐up messages — all without a human on the line. It isn’t a voicemail box. It actually talks back, asks questions, and can understand context 24/7.

## How It Works

When someone calls and you’re busy, the AI picks up and says, “Thanks for calling [Your Business]. How can I help?” It then gathers the caller’s name, address, what they need, and when they need it. It books the appointment straight into your calendar. If the query is beyond its scope (e.g., a complex complaint), it flags it and sends you a summary via SMS or email so you can follow up.

## Who Benefits Most

- **Tradies** (plumbers, electricians, HVAC): you’re under a sink or on a ladder and can’t answer the phone.
- **Property managers**: emergency tenant calls after hours.
- **Dental/medical clinics**: front‐desk staff overwhelmed with appointment bookings.
- **Real‐estate agents**: open‐house enquiries flood in.

In each case, missed calls mean lost jobs, delayed service, and frustrated customers.

## What It Costs

I won’t give you a price here because every business is different, and I price each setup individually. What I can say is that the AI receptionist usually pays for itself on the first recovered call‐out if you’ve ever missed a high‐value job because you couldn’t answer the phone.

## Honest Limitations

It handles routine calls exceptionally well but doesn’t replace human judgment for complex, emotional, or legally sensitive conversations. Think of it as handling the overflow – the calls that come in while you’re actually working.
